examples.description: Early-stage SaaS founder with multiple marketing tasks

founder.name: Alex Chen
founder.summary: Alex is a technical founder building a B2B SaaS productivity tool. Currently at MVP stage with 5 beta users. Strong engineering background but limited marketing experience.

tasks.title: Launch on Product Hunt
tasks.description: Create PH launch strategy and assets

input.contextNotes: Need revenue within 2 months or will run out of runway

expectedOutput.executiveSummary: Focus on revenue-critical tasks first. Given 2-month runway constraint, prioritize billing infrastructure and conversion optimization before growth experiments. Sequence: Fix bleeding (onboarding bugs) → Enable revenue (Stripe) → Drive traffic (Product Hunt launch).

topPriorities.rationale: No billing = no revenue. This is the most critical blocker to monetization. With 2-month runway, every day without payment capability is lost opportunity. Technical founder can implement this within 1 week using Stripe's excellent docs.
preworkRequired: Define pricing tiers (simple: single tier to start)
Set up Stripe account and testing
Design minimal billing UI mockups
successMetrics: First paid customer within 48 hours of launch

topPriorities.rationale: 40% drop-off is hemorrhaging potential revenue. Quick wins here compound with every new user. As technical founder, this plays to your strengths. Fix before driving more traffic via Product Hunt.
preworkRequired: Add analytics to identify exact drop-off points
Interview 2 users who dropped off (if possible)
Test signup flow on multiple browsers
successMetrics: Zero console errors in signup flow

topPriorities.description: Create PH launch strategy and assets
topPriorities.rationale: High-leverage traffic driver, but only after billing and onboarding are solid. One shot to make a splash - need infrastructure ready to convert traffic to revenue. Time launch for Tuesday or Wednesday.
preworkRequired: Create compelling hero image and demo video
Line up 5-10 supporters for launch day upvotes
Prepare FAQ responses for comments
Ensure billing and onboarding are bulletproof

topPriorities.rationale: SEO is long-term play (3-6 months to see results). With 2-month runway, this is lower priority than direct revenue drivers. Consider after securing initial revenue stream.
preworkRequired: Identify 3 high-intent keywords using Ahrefs/Ubersuggest
Outline posts targeting bottom-of-funnel searches
Consider hiring freelance writer ($50-100/post)
successMetrics: 5+ organic visits per post within 30 days

topPriorities.rationale: Important for platform positioning but high effort for uncertain near-term return. Defer until you have paying customers requesting integrations. Validate demand first.
preworkRequired: Survey existing users: who needs API access?
Define 3 most valuable integration use cases
Scope minimal API surface area
successMetrics: Validated use cases with revenue potential

schedule.focus: Stop the bleeding - fix conversion blockers
risksToWatch: Bugs take longer than expected - timebox to 4 days max
Stripe integration complexity - use Stripe Checkout for speed
Launch timing - avoid Fridays and holidays
Low conversion from PH traffic - have retargeting ready
Distraction - stay focused on revenue-generating activities

risks.description: 2-month runway creates time pressure that may lead to cutting corners on quality
risks.mitigation: Timebox all tasks strictly. If Stripe takes >1 week, use simpler solution like Gumroad temporarily.

risks.description: Product Hunt may not convert to revenue if product-market fit is weak
risks.mitigation: Do 5 customer interviews this week to validate value prop. Adjust messaging before launch.

risks.description: Solo founder wearing all hats - risk of burnout or dropping balls
risks.mitigation: Cut scope ruthlessly. Consider hiring freelancer for PH assets ($200-500). Sleep 7+ hours.

risks.description: Onboarding bugs may be deeper than expected (infrastructure issues)
risks.mitigation: Timebox debugging to 4 days. If not resolved, consider complete signup flow rewrite with simpler approach.

nextSteps: TODAY: Set up analytics on signup flow to identify exact drop-off points
TODAY: Create Stripe account and read integration docs
Tomorrow: Fix top onboarding bug (should take <4 hours)
This week: Interview 2 users who completed onboarding successfully - what almost stopped them?
This week: Define single pricing tier ($29/mo is good starting point for B2B SaaS)

examples.description: Agency owner trying to transition to product

founder.name: Maria Santos
founder.summary: Maria runs a profitable design agency ($30k/mo revenue) and wants to build a productized design service. She has a team of 3 designers but limited technical resources. Strong client relationships but new to product thinking.

tasks.title: Hire engineer to build product
tasks.description: Need technical co-founder or senior engineer

tasks.title: Build no-code MVP
tasks.description: Use Webflow + Airtable for product prototype

tasks.title: Hire sales person
tasks.description: Scale agency revenue to fund product development

documents.summary: 5 clients mentioned wanting faster turnaround times. 3 clients asked for fixed monthly pricing instead of hourly. Clients love quality but frustrated by project scoping calls.
keyInsights: Pain point: Scoping overhead for small tasks
Demand signal: Fixed pricing strongly preferred

input.contextNotes: Agency is profitable but I'm tired of client services. Want to build something scalable.

expectedOutput.executiveSummary: Bridge to product through productized service, not technology first. Your clients are already asking for subscription design - this is validated demand. Capture this revenue immediately to fund future product development. Avoid hiring engineer until you've proven product-market fit with service.

topPriorities.rationale: Your clients are literally asking for this. Productized design subscriptions are proven ($10k-20k/mo per client). This leverages your existing strengths (design, client relationships) and generates cash flow to fund future product work. Can launch in 2 weeks vs 6+ months for software product.
preworkRequired: Analyze last 20 client projects: what's most requested?
Define service tiers (suggest: $5k/mo unlimited, $10k/mo priority)
Create simple service page on existing website
Identify 3 existing clients to migrate first
successMetrics: Convert 2 existing clients to subscription within 30 days

topPriorities.rationale: Validate product concept before hiring expensive engineers. Use no-code tools to test core workflow with existing subscription clients. If they won't pay for manual service, they won't pay for automated product. This de-risks future tech investment.
preworkRequired: Define core workflow: what would product automate?
Sketch 5 key screens/features
Learn Webflow basics (20 hours of tutorials)
Set up Airtable as backend database
successMetrics: 3 subscription clients using MVP for real projects
Identified top 5 features they'd pay extra for
Validated willingness to pay for software ($99-299/mo)

topPriorities.rationale: Once subscription offering is packaged, sales leverage makes sense. Part-time SDR or commission-only closer can scale revenue while you focus on product transition. But only after offer is proven - need clear pitch and pricing first.
preworkRequired: Document sales process: how do you close clients today?
Create sales deck for subscription service
Close 5 subscription clients yourself to refine pitch
Define ideal customer profile and lead sources
successMetrics: Sales hire closes 2 new clients in first month
Your time freed up by 20+ hours/week

topPriorities.rationale: DEFER until you've validated product concept with no-code MVP and have consistent $30k+/mo subscription revenue to fund salary. Hiring engineer now is premature - high cost, high risk, wrong sequence. Prove demand first.
preworkRequired: Validate product concept with 10+ paying users on no-code MVP
Define clear product requirements document
Have 6 months runway to pay engineer salary
Decide: hire vs co-founder vs outsource vs no-code long-term?
successMetrics: Clear ROI model: engineer cost vs product revenue potential

risksToWatch: Overthinking offering - ship simple version first
Client objections - be ready to adjust pricing
Tutorial paralysis - focus on building, not learning
Scope creep - limit to 3 features max

milestones: 2 clients using MVP for real projects
risksToWatch: No adoption - identify friction points quickly
Hiring wrong person - start with trial project

risks.description: Spreading too thin between agency operations and product development
risks.mitigation: Delegate agency operations to senior designer. Block 15 hours/week for product work. Consider reducing agency client load by 30%.

risks.description: Product concept may not resonate even though service does - different value propositions
risks.mitigation: Start with hybrid: subscription service with software tools, not pure product. Transition gradually.

risks.description: Agency cash flow disruption could kill product runway
risks.mitigation: Maintain 6 months operating expenses in cash. Don't reduce agency revenue until product revenue is proven.

nextSteps: TODAY: Email 5 best clients: 'Considering a subscription design service - would you be interested?'
This week: Analyze last 20 projects to identify most common request patterns
This week: Create simple pricing page for subscription service (use Carrd or existing site)
Next week: Schedule 3 sales calls with interested clients
Next week: Sign up for Webflow and complete first tutorial project
